identificationModule.briefTitle: Comparison Between Vaginal Pessary and Progestogen in Twin Pregnancy With Short Cervical Length
identificationModule.officialTitle: Randomised Controlled Trial Comparing Vaginal Pessary and Progestogen as an Intervention in Twin Pregnancy With Short Cervical Length to Prevent Spontaneous Preterm Birth

descriptionModule.briefSummary: A randomized clinical trial comparing vaginal progestogen and vaginal pessary as an intervention for twin pregnancies with short cervical length.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: This is a randomized controlled trial to compare women with twin pregnancies and diagnosed with asymptomatic short cervical length. Two types of interventions will be compared i.e vaginal progestogen and vaginal pessary.

designInfo.interventionModelDescription: All women with twin pregnancies will be screened for suitability via measurement of the cervical length at 20 to 24 weeks gestation. Those with a cervical length of 30mm or less will be recruited into the study.

armGroups.label: Vaginal progestogen
armGroups.description: 200mg of vaginal progestogen will be inserted before bedtime every day from time of recruitment until 34 weeks gestation.

armGroups.label: Vaginal pessary
armGroups.description: Vaginal pessary with an internal diameter size of 32 or 35 mm will be inserted at the time of recruitment and kept until 34 weeks gestation.

interventions.name: Micronised vaginal progesterone
interventions.description: A diary will be given to participants to ensure compliance.

interventions.name: Vaginal pessary
interventions.description: The internal diameter size will be decided based on the clinical assessment of the cervix.

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* all twin pregnancies
* cervical length less than 30mm

Exclusion Criteria:

* Twin to twin transfusion syndrome
* Stillbirth
* congenital anomaly in one of the fetuses
* previous cervical trauma or surgery
* cervical cerclage in current pregnancy
* premature labour with or without rupture of membranes
* severe vaginal discharge
* acute vaginitis or cervicitis
